newsitem.title: CHINA: China says to use subsidies for unleaded gasoline.
newsitem.headline: China says to use subsidies for unleaded gasoline.

text.p: China's environmental protection agency has recommended using subsidies to promote the use of unleaded gasoline as part of a programme to phase out leaded fuel by 2000, an environmental official said on Wednesday.

"We have given several recommendations to government authorities for them to choose," said Li Pei, project officer at the National Environmental Protection Agency of China's air pollution control division.
"All of them involve subsidies of some form," she told Reuters in an interview.
Beijing will begin phasing out leaded gasoline next month with petrol stations in the city centre starting to switch to unleaded gasoline only.
Authorities want to make unleaded gasoline cheaper than leaded gasoline. Unleaded gasoline now costs about five percent more than leaded gasoline.
Both the Finance Ministry and the Tax Bureau have been consulted on the plans, Li said, adding that the environmental agency hoped a plan would be in place by the end of the year.
"We don't want this to affect tax revenues or discourage production by the refiners," she said.
Beijing plans to start with some 300 of the capital's 800 gas stations, switching them station by station to selling only unleaded fuel.
Unleaded gasoline is currently sold at only 15 of the capital's filling stations, Li said.
By next year, all stations in Beijing will be selling only the unleaded variety.
Li said that the plan calls for the big northern city of Tianjin to shift this year. Shanghai and Guangzhou will soon be added to the list and implementation will be nationwide by the year 2000.
